arguments.value: Victor Marrero, born in 1941 in Santurce, Puerto Rico, is a United States District Judge for the Southern District of New York who was nominated by President William J. Clinton in 1999 and assumed senior status in 2010. He earned a B.A. from New York University in 1964 and an LL.B. from Yale Law School in 1968. Earlier in his career, he held a series of public service positions in New York City and State, worked in private practice in New York City, and later served as a U.S. ambassador to the Economic and Social Council of the United Nations and as permanent representative of the United States to the Organization of American States.
